census.leverage_ratio_note: (401 generated code + 919 generated docs) / (225 metadata + 869 generator+provider) = 1.21x, up from 0.38x. The numerator grew because `meta docs` had never been run despite the project configuring a docs surface; the denominator dropped 202 lines of dead scaffolded generator. Still a low number for a MetaObjects adopter, and still the right number: smon's return is a loader-enforced vocabulary plus four gates, not code volume.

closed.how: `.metaobjects/.gitignore` line 1 changed from `.gen-state/` to `.gen-state/*` + `!.gen-state/.hashes.json`, and the 16-line manifest is committed. THE TOOL FOUND THIS, not the reviewer: rc.4's `meta gen` printed the whole diagnosis unprompted, including the git subtlety that a negation under a bare excluded DIRECTORY can never apply. It also unblocked `verify --codegen`, which needs that manifest to distinguish a hand-edited generated file from a clean tree on a machine that did not generate it.

new.title: the Verdict.status member set was spelled three times in hand-written code; 1.0 gave it a runtime artifact and the project now derives all three
new.evidence: rc.4 emits `export const VerdictStatusEnum = z.enum(["OK","WARN","FAIL"])` for an INLINE field.enum — through 0.15.x only a package-level shared enum got a named artifact. Before that existed, runner.ts spelled the members inside VERDICT_LINE_PATTERN's regex alternation AND again in `isVerdictStatus`, and cli.ts twice restated the union as an inline type. Adding a fourth status to @values would have left the parser rejecting it as FAIL/BAD_VERDICT — a wrong-but-plausible verdict, not an error.
new.impact: Both spellings retired. PROVEN in both directions on a throwaway copy: adding "DEGRADED" to @values and re-running `meta gen` made the parser accept `verdict: DEGRADED …` with ZERO hand-written lines changed; re-hardcoding "OK|WARN|FAIL" back into runner.ts makes the new test fail with the received value literally `BAD_VERDICT`. COST: importing a zod value into the CLI's module graph grew dist/smon.js from 61.5 KB / 39 modules to 181.6 KB / 58 modules (startup unchanged at 0.01-0.02s, below noise). Taken deliberately.
new.parity_gate: test/parser.test.ts 'every declared Verdict.status member parses (the set is derived from the model)' — iterates VerdictStatusEnum.options, so it passes untouched when a member is added and fails when the list is re-hardcoded

new.title: generated code imported zod and the manifest never declared it; it resolved only through a tool package's transitive dependency
new.evidence: `grep zod package.json` was empty while every generated value-object file starts `import { z } from "zod"`. It resolved because @metaobjectsdev/sdk carries a real `dependencies: { zod: ^3.23.0 }` that the installer hoists to node_modules/zod, and @metaobjectsdev/runtime-ts declares zod as an OPTIONAL peer — `peerDependenciesMeta.zod.optional === true` — so there is no install warning either.
new.impact: Latent, not visible: bun/npm hoisting hides it, a strict layout would not, and it breaks the day `sdk` stops depending on zod. Fixed here by declaring `zod: ^3.25.76`. The upstream half is that nothing told the project: `meta init` learned to declare what generated output imports, but an ALREADY-initialized project gets no such signal from any command or gate.

new.title: namesFile() is wired and emits zero files, silently — correctly, because smon has no physical database names at all
new.evidence: With namesFile() wired, `meta gen` reports the same 14 files and no *.names.ts exists anywhere. Confirmed from the generator's own source: pass 1 is `ctx.entities.filter(ctx.matches)` over 'every matched object that participates in the database (#248)', and every smon object is a sourceless object.value. There is no message either way.
new.impact: A Names-constant conversion is a VERIFIED no-op for this project: zero physical table/column/schema/index names exist to convert, and `git grep` finds no SQL of any kind. Kept wired so the artifact appears by itself if an object ever gains a source.rdb.

new.title: the 1.0 agent/ docs surface emits nothing for this project and says nothing about why, while the AGENTS.md it just scaffolded tells the reader to go read those pages
new.evidence: Adding "agent" to docs.surfaces changes `meta docs` output by nothing: '1 overview + 7 entity page(s) + 3 template page(s); 12 api page(s)'. No agent/ directory. Run meta docs', and running it produces nothing and explains nothing.
